collar_policy.rule: hard constraint 4: dots must satisfy d_cat >= 3.0 px
collar_policy.applies_to: all three variants identically, so it is not the axis

mechanism_card.hypothesis: The brief-literal MASS rule: R0 carries mass that does not pay, and the parent's own FIFO-BFS thinning order is an acceptable proxy for 'least useful first'.
mechanism_card.mechanism: DTI = T/(0.2T + 0.2(S-M) + 0.8|G|): a dot within 3 px of hidden truth adds up to 1.0 to T and only (1 - max k) to the penalty S-M, while a dot further than 3 px adds nothing to T and a full 1.0 to S-M. Mass is therefore not neutral: every non-paying dot costs 0.2 of denominator, and T is a max-plus quantity, so a dot whose kernel disc is already claimed by a neighbour supplies no unique credit at all. Both variants test that algebra at constant placement and constant collar. Removal order is the reversed H19-5 FIFO-BFS visit rank (the documented d2.8 thinning tie-break). Measured against the parent's own support, the removed dots average 2.04 unique kernel credit versus 2.01 for the dots kept: the FIFO tail is NOT a redundancy ordering, so this file is effectively a spatially arbitrary 20% mass cut. That is the point of pairing it with uniq20 at identical count.
mechanism_card.non_fault_mimic: Thin, isolated H19-5 support is produced as readily by road/rail corridors, DEM artefacts, lithologic contacts and drainage as by short fault strands, so 'redundant' and 'noise' are not the same set. Removing duplicate dots can equally delete the second strand of a real step-over, which the 3 px kernel cannot distinguish.

mechanism_card.falsifier: Because the dropped set is nearly unbiased in unique credit, a live gain >= +0.01 here would mean mass matters and dot choice does not; a live drop <= -0.01 would mean R0's dots are paying and mass reduction is the wrong direction for every selection rule.
mechanism_card.structural_geologist_note: Check whether the removed dots concentrate on one structural trend or region; the patch statistics say 10311 of 26645 support patches lose every dot.
